source.publisher: Ulster Herald (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: two nominations (Michael Ward and Patrick Conway); 'Mr. Patrick Conway ... has withdrawn his nomination, giving Mr. Michael Ward an unopposed return for the Mullaghslin division' (Ulster Herald, 29 April 1939, p. 5)

note: Triennial election of the Omagh rural district councillors, 1939. Nominations closed on Tuesday 18 April 1939. Thirty-five divisions received nominations; the only double nomination, Mullaghslin, ended with Patrick Conway's withdrawal, and 'There will be no contests in Omagh Rural district' (Ulster Herald, 29 April 1939, p. 5). In Drumquin, Fintona, Sluggan and Liffer no nominations were received and the previous members are 'deemed to have been re-elected' (Ulster Herald, 22 April 1939, p. 5). No party labels are printed in the list. No poll was held; the folder date is the provisional Tyrone polling day. Previous member H. K. M'Aleer, M.P., retired. Patrick Conway was nominated and withdrew. Returned unopposed.
